strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine computational challenges in agentic system optimization
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with ablation studies demonstrating the value of each design component
Consistent improvements across three diverse domains (code generation, math reasoning, task reasoning)
Clear presentation with effective figures and well-structured methodology
Thorough analysis of label efficiency showing benefits of pretraining in low-data regimes
Sensible multi-view design combining complementary information sources (graph, code, prompts)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: multi-view encoding is straightforward concatenation of standard encoders with basic MLP aggregation; pretraining uses standard reconstruction + contrastive objectives
Critical technical inconsistency: contrastive pretraining requires success labels for positive pairs, contradicting the 'unlabeled' claim; this fundamental issue needs clarification
Modest empirical improvements: 9.97% average accuracy gain and 6.74% utility gain, with downstream optimization benefit of only 3.4% (71% to 74.43%)

Weak baseline comparisons: primarily adapted from NAS literature rather than workflow-specific methods; no direct comparison with claimed superior alternatives (FLORA-Bench, MAS-GPT); missing simple baselines (linear models, decision trees)
Unclear technical details: multi-graph construction (Gprompt, Gcode, Goperator) not rigorously defined; simple MLP decoder may not effectively teach useful representations
Limited reproducibility: only AFlow subset of FLORA-Bench used (not public), proprietary embeddings required, no code release mentioned, small scale (30-42 workflows per domain)

Restricted evaluation scope: binary classification only (pass/fail), not continuous performance metrics; significant performance drops in transferability experiments (13.37% on HotpotQA); results may not generalize beyond FLORA-Bench
Insufficient analysis: no error analysis or visualization of learned representations, no study of what each view learns, case studies only show code examples not predictor behavior
Potential data leakage: unclear whether pretraining data is completely isolated from test sets

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem addressing computational bottleneck in agentic system optimization
Thoughtfully designed multi-view workflow encoding combining graph, code, and prompt representations with solid ablation validation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with consistent improvements (up to 12.12% accuracy, 15.16% utility) across three domains
Principled approach to data scarcity through cross-domain unsupervised pretraining with convincing low-data regime analysis
Clear presentation and writing with reproducible experimental setup using established benchmarks
Systematic ablations demonstrating the necessity of each design component (Tables 4-5)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines established techniques (multi-view learning, GNNs, contrastive pretraining) without fundamental algorithmic insights

Severely constrained evaluation scope: single benchmark (FLORA-Bench AFlow), only 30-42 workflows per domain with 5-6 nodes, no cross-generation evaluation across different workflow generation methods
Binary classification fundamentally limits applicability: cannot predict continuous performance metrics or cost/latency tradeoffs, only pass/fail
Unclear practical efficiency gains: Table 6 shows $0 search cost for all methods making comparison uninformative; actual number of LLM calls saved not quantified
Pretraining procedure uses ground-truth labels for positive pairs in contrastive learning, contradicting the motivation of scarce labeled data; data split management unclear
Oversimplified code representation using basic MLP without modern code embedding methods; task encoder analysis missing; aggregation is crude concatenation
Weak baseline comparisons: MLP baseline is trivial, no direct quantitative comparison to FLORA-Bench's method or MAS-GPT, no statistical significance testing
Limited generalization analysis: single workflow family (AFlow), poor transferability to unseen domains (13.37% accuracy on HotpotQA), no cross-architecture evaluation
No failure case analysis or prediction confidence estimation; unclear why approach fails on certain domains; optimization uses only simple random search without efficiency comparison

strengths: Addresses a practical and underexplored problem of efficient agentic workflow evaluation with clear computational motivation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including thorough ablations on multi-view designs (Tables 4-5), label efficiency analysis (Figure 3), OOD generalization, and LLM backbone robustness

Well-motivated multi-view encoding scheme capturing complementary workflow aspects (graph structure, code semantics, prompt specifications) with convincing ablations demonstrating their synergistic value
Effective data-efficient pretraining strategy using contrastive and reconstruction objectives, showing meaningful benefits in low-label regimes (73% vs 70% at 0.1 ratio)
Significant practical efficiency gains over LLM-based approaches at inference time (0.054ms vs 2,000+ ms per sample), enabling scalable search
Extensive supplementary analyses including cross-domain OOD tests, multiple GNN backbone ablations, and comparative evaluation against LLM predictors
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (multi-view learning, contrastive pretraining, standard encoders) without introducing fundamental methodological innovations

Modest empirical improvements with overlapping error bars: average accuracy gains of only 2.05% and utility gains of 3.79%; no statistical significance testing provided despite tight standard deviations

Evaluation restricted to single benchmark (FLORA-Bench only): restricts generalizability claims; significant OOD performance drops (18-24% across systems) suggest the method learns benchmark-specific patterns rather than generalizable features
Restrictive problem formulation: binary success/failure classification is coarse-grained; practitioners need finer-grained continuous performance predictions for meaningful optimization guidance

Weak out-of-distribution generalization: cross-system accuracy drops from 79.97% to 62% (AFlow→G-Designer), indicating non-transferable learning of framework-specific patterns and limiting practical deployment

Unclear practical value: the method is search-agnostic but only evaluated with random search; lacks integration with actual optimization algorithms (genetic algorithms, Bayesian optimization); workflow optimization results (Table 13) relegated to appendix despite being central to impact
Imbalanced pretraining setup: unlabeled corpus contains 90.58% reasoning vs. 6.56% code tasks; domain transfer effectiveness not analyzed; pretraining gains diminish at higher label ratios
Task encoder design underexplored: critical component concatenating T5/BERT embeddings lacks ablation study; unclear how much performance depends on this design vs. multi-view encoding
Missing error analysis and failure characterization: no investigation of which workflow types the predictor struggles with; no guidance on when the method is applicable
Questionable label scarcity claim: benchmark contains 739-1,400 workflows; 0.5 label ratio yields 370-700 labeled samples, which is not particularly scarce for modern deep learning

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing real computational bottleneck in agentic workflow evaluation
Thoughtfully designed multi-view representation (graph, code, prompt) with clear complementary benefits
Exceptionally comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning multiple domains, ablations, OOD settings, and label efficiency analysis
Consistent and strong empirical results across all evaluated domains (2-7% accuracy improvements, 3-6% utility improvements)
Effective solution to label scarcity through cross-domain unsupervised pretraining with demonstrated practical benefits
Excellent practical efficiency gains over LLM-based prediction (orders of magnitude faster with break-even economics)
Rigorous ablations validating design choices (Tables 4-5) and supporting reproducibility (Algorithm 1, implementation details)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily applies existing techniques (multi-view learning, contrastive pretraining, GNNs) to new domain without algorithmic innovation
Evaluation restricted to single benchmark (FLORA-Bench); no independent validation on other agentic workflow benchmarks
Incomplete baseline comparisons: no direct comparison with FLORA-Bench's own FLORA method; LLM baseline uses weak 5-shot prompting
Significant out-of-distribution performance degradation (17.9% drop in cross-system generalization) with limited error analysis
Binary classification limitation reduces practical applicability; practitioners need graded performance estimates and task-specific metrics
Insufficient analysis of learned representations: no attention visualization, view contribution analysis, or failure case studies
Cross-domain pretraining data heavily skewed (90.58% Reasoning) with unclear whether improvements stem from data quantity vs. genuine transfer
Limited search algorithm evaluation: only demonstrates random sampling + ranking, not integration with sophisticated optimization methods
Graph reconstruction design choice (stop-gradient for graph vs. input space for others) lacks clear justification
Task encoder design underspecified with no ablation on encoder choice or impact on overall performance
